Diagnostic.description:
One structured finding produced while loading a persisted artifact.

Field names and enum representations are a persisted JSON contract. Unknown
fields are rejected during deserialization.

actual_version.description: Version found in the payload, when one was present.

artifact_hash.description: Canonical artifact digest, including its algorithm prefix, when available.

contract.description: Stable persisted contract identifier, when the finding is contract-specific.

expected_version.description: Version expected by the loader, when version context is available.

instrument_id.description: Instrument identifier associated with the finding, when available.

message.description: Human-readable explanation with source details such as parse line and column.

phase.description: Loading stage that produced the finding.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer locating the finding in the source document, when known.

position_id.description: Portfolio-position identifier associated with the finding, when available.

revision_id.description: Storage revision identifier associated with the artifact, when available.

severity.description: Whether the finding is fatal or recoverable.

LoadPhase.description: Stage of persisted artifact loading that produced a diagnostic.

oneOf.description: Source bytes were parsed into a JSON document.
Contract identity and version policy were checked.
A supported older payload was migrated.
Document shape and required fields were checked.
Domain invariants and references were checked.
The validated artifact was converted to canonical JSON bytes.
A content digest was calculated or checked.
Runtime domain objects were built from the validated payload.

Severity.description: Severity assigned to a persisted artifact diagnostic.

oneOf.description: A finding that prevents successful loading.
A recoverable finding that callers should inspect.

description: Bounded structured diagnostics emitted by persisted-contract validation.

diagnostics.description: Individual findings retained up to the configured diagnostic limit.

truncated.description:
Whether one or more additional findings were omitted due to the limit.

A truncated report with no retained diagnostics is treated as fatal
because the wire format cannot distinguish omitted warnings from errors.

title: Validation Report
